notes: Read SKILL.md in full; it is the only file. Cloudflare Zero Trust guidance: installing cloudflared, creating and routing a Cloudflare Tunnel, ingress config, running it under systemd/Docker, Access applications and policies via the Cloudflare API, service tokens, device posture, Gateway DNS filtering, WARP enrollment/split tunnels and browser SSH.

Following it installs cloudflared (brew, Cloudflare's signed apt repository, or docker pull at SKILL.md:32-40), authenticates with `cloudflared tunnel login`, creates tunnels and DNS CNAME records, installs a systemd service, and calls the live Cloudflare API with $CF_API_TOKEN to create Access apps, policies, service tokens and Gateway rules (SKILL.md:154-260). Medium because it uses real account credentials and changes the user's Cloudflare and DNS configuration; acceptable because every action is within the user's own Zero Trust setup that the skill is invoked for, with placeholder IDs the user must supply.

The sample ingress for the internal wiki sets `originRequest: noTLSVerify: true` (SKILL.md:82-83) without explanation; the origin is plain http://localhost:8080 so it has no effect there, but users should not copy it to HTTPS origins. Service-token secrets are environment variables/placeholders. Related Skills links (SKILL.md:342-345: ../cloudflare-workers/, ../../networking/dns-management/, ../../networking/reverse-proxy/, ../../networking/service-mesh/) are optional pointers that do not ship with this skill. Frontmatter declares license: MIT.
